issues.description: Inefficient string-contains: Uses substring in a loop, leading to O(N*M) complexity and excessive allocations. Most Scheme implementations provide a more efficient built-in or SRFI utility.
Weak Assertions: emit-multiple-test only asserts that the result is a string, which is a very weak test. It should verify that the output actually contains the expected lines.
Inconsistent Indentation: The indentation in the string-contains helper deviates from the 2-space convention used elsewhere in the project.

files_reviewed.notes: Well-structured test file with good coverage of DSL features. Minor efficiency and style issues in helper function. Some tests could have stronger assertions.

issues.description: Primitive Misuse: Uses legacy 'choice' and 'choose-n' from persona-prompt-gen.ss instead of the modern 'pick' and 'pick-n' from the Enhanced Persona DSL (persona-dsl.ss). This creates architectural fragmentation.
Manual String Formatting: Uses brittle string-append and manual bullet points instead of structured emit-list and emit-section procedures provided by the new DSL.
Unsafe List Access: Accessing items with (car profiling-approaches) and (cadr profiling-approaches) assumes choose-n always returns at least two items. Fragile pattern.

files_reviewed.notes: Functional persona definition but uses legacy DSL primitives instead of the newer Enhanced Persona DSL. Should be migrated to use modern constructs for consistency.

issues.description: Model Inconsistency: The 'model' field is set to 'opencode/big-pickle', but JavaScript invokers (like invoke-pedagogue.js) hardcode 'sonnet'. This makes global model configuration impossible via YAML.
Tier Contradiction: The YAML defines 'tier: haiku', but llm-agent-poll.ss hardcodes 'tier: shepherd' when writing posts.
Documentation Gap: Comments describe a process pool logic (square root of persona count) that is not implemented in the provided polling scripts.

files_reviewed.notes: Configuration file has good structure but contains values that are not actually used by the system. Model and tier settings are overridden by hardcoded values in the invokers.

issues.description: Inconsistent Tagging: The SYSTEM_PROMPT instructs the agent to tag others using full names. Every other agent in the system uses short names like @opus. This inconsistency likely breaks cross-agent triggers.
Command Injection Risk: Using execSync with a template literal for the shell command is dangerous. Should use spawnSync or the 'input' option for better security.
Cleanup Failure: fs.unlinkSync(promptFile) is outside the catch block. If execSync fails, the temp file is never deleted, leading to /tmp pollution.
Misleading Header: The JSDoc says the agent 'samples from multiple models,' but the implementation only uses 'sonnet'.

files_reviewed.notes: Has security concerns with command execution and resource cleanup issues. Documentation is misleading about multi-model sampling.

issues.description: Stderr Leakage: The shell command uses 2>&1, which merges stderr into the response string. This causes internal log messages to be included in the final forum/chat post and breaks error detection logic.
Global Depth Counter: The bot-message-count.txt file is global for all agents and threads. Concurrent conversations will share the same counter, causing premature truncation.
Race Condition: save-count! deletes and then writes the state file. This is not atomic; concurrent pollers will encounter file-not-found errors or reset each other's counts.
Incomplete JSON Escaping: escape-json only handles quotes, backslashes, and newlines. It fails to escape other control characters (tabs, carriage returns), resulting in invalid JSON.
Inefficient String Operations: string-join uses string-append in loops, resulting in O(N^2) complexity.
Temp File Collisions: shell-command-to-string uses current-milliseconds for temp filenames, which can collide in high-concurrency environments.

files_reviewed.notes: Critical issues with stderr handling, race conditions, and incomplete JSON escaping. The global depth counter design is fundamentally flawed for concurrent operation.

summary: Gemini Flash QA review identified 18 issues across 5 files. Most critical issues are in llm-agent-poll.ss (4 high-severity bugs including stderr leakage, race conditions, and incomplete JSON escaping) and invoke-pedagogue.js (2 high-severity issues with command injection risk and inconsistent tagging). The velocity-dsl.ss uses legacy DSL primitives instead of the newer Enhanced Persona DSL. The defaults.yaml configuration is not properly consumed by the invokers, with hardcoded values overriding the YAML settings.
